sentences.text:
Through: Mr. Sukhmeet Singh, 
 Petitioners in perso  versus  THE STATE OF NCT & ANR. .
 Through: Mr. Raj Kumar, APP f  with SI Naveen, P.S.
 Mr.Praveen Chaturved  R-2 with R-2 in pers  CORAM:
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJNISH BHATNAGAR  ORDER % 23.03.2023 CRL.M.A. 7657/2023 (Exemption) Exemption allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
The application stands disposed of.

1. This is a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of FIR No. 130/2021, under Sections 498A/406/506/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Rajouri Garden, and all proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.
Learned APP appears on advance notice, and accepts notice.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 got married on 02.04.1995 according to Sikh rites and customs and they lived together as husband and wife with each other and two children were born out of the said wedlock.
On 11.02.2021, the respondent No.2 got the above said FIR registered against the petitioners.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the trial, with the intervention of elderly persons, the respondent no. 2 and petitioner no. 1 have settled the matter amicably in terms of the Settlement Agreement dated 13.09.2022.
He further submitted that there are no pending disputes between them.
Copy of the said settlement is placed on record.
5. Petitioners and respondent no.2 are present in Court today and they have been identified by their counsels.
I have interacted with the parties and they submit that they have settled their disputes.

Respondent no.2 admits that she has settled the matter amicably with the petitioner no. 1 and she is Gurdeep Singh & Anr vs The State Of Nct & Anr on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53350816/
1 living happily with her husband since the day of lodging of this FIR.

entities.text: Gurdeep Singh & Anr vs The State Of Nct & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She further submits that the settlement/compromise has taken place voluntarily, without any force, pressure or coercion.
Respondent no.2 submits that nothing remains to be adjudicated further between them and she has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.

6. Learned APP for the State submits that in view of the settlement and as the petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 are living happily together, the State has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
7. Keeping in view the above facts and circumstances, since the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, no useful purpose will be served by keeping the case pending.
It will be nothing but abuse of the process of law.

Consequentially, this petition is allowed and FIR No. 130/2021,
under Section 498A/406/506/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Rajouri Garden, and all proceedings emanating therefrom shall stand quashed qua the petitioners.
8.
The present petition stands disposed of accordingly.
RAJNISH BHATNAGAR, J MARCH 23, 2023/ib
